title: Turning at the backward boundary
statement: Let $W$ and $M$ be finite binary Turing machines, let $a$ be a natural number, and let $x$ be a finite word over the schedule alphabet. Let $c$ be a schedule configuration, $u\in\mathbb{Z}$, $R\in\mathbb{N}$, a finite data register $d$, data-tape contents $T$, and output word $o$. Assume the guide tape of $c$ is the fixed guide of radius $R$. One step from the backward phase at guide position $-R-1$ enters the return-center phase at position $-R$, leaving the base configuration, $u$, data register, data tapes, and output unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Data register $d$, data-tape contents $T$, and output word $o$
Guide tape of $c$ equals the radius-$R$ guide
replaced:
Suppose the base's guide tape is the fixed guide of radius $R$.  From the
backward phase with guide head at $-R - 1$, one simulator step enters the return
phase at position $-R$ and leaves the finite data register, data tapes, and
